subject: Post-call: throughput matrix & stream segmentation for pilot
messages:
From: Emma Liu <emma@velocitypay.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-14T15:12:00Z
Subject: Intro call follow-up: workload shape and SLOs

Hi Olga / Marissa — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap from our side and the data points we promised to share: 

- Primary flow: real-time payment review assistant called by our customer support reps during calls. Each session sends streaming prompts (interleaved transcription + user messages). Typical session: 40–150 tokens per turn, median 6 turns.
- Traffic profile: baseline steady QPS ~8 requests/sec during business hours; two short crests per day for 7–12 minutes hitting 60–85 requests/sec (mostly short streaming sessions).
- Token volume: average session token generation ~2.2k tokens; peak sessions (5% of sessions) ~8–12k tokens.
- Concurrency: concurrent active streams typically 18–25 sustained; crest concurrency spikes to ~180 for 7–12 minutes.
- Latency SLO: P95 end-to-end for streaming-first-token target 350ms; P99 we’d like <800ms for 512-token windows (we can be flexible if you explain trade-offs).
- Failure sensitivity: for any degraded latency we need deterministic fallback (cached summary or reduced model).

Next asks for Redwood:
1) Can you sketch a recommended pilot capacity (GPU slots / conservative QPS headroom) for a 90-day pilot to handle crest behavior and maintain the SLO?
2) Do you need raw tokenized logs or samples? We can provide pre-tokenized examples + session traces.
3) Any constraints around streaming keepalive/idle timeouts that would impact our integration?

I’ll attach a CSV with hourly QPS distribution and a small sample session trace in a follow-up email.

Thanks,
Emma
Emma Liu
Sr. Product Manager, VelocityPay

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Liu <emma@velocitypay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-14T18:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Intro call follow-up: workload shape and SLOs

Emma — thanks for the clear summary and the distribution preview on the call. Attaching an initial throughput matrix (throughput_matrix_vp.xlsx) and a sample stream profile JSON (stream_profile_samples.json) that shows how we translate crest vs steady-state into capacity slots. High-level notes below; full sizing rationale is in the spreadsheet.

High-level sizing assumptions (first-pass):
- Model family: recommend running pilot on a 13B quantized variant to balance latency / cost given your session lengths.
- Steady-state: sustain ~8 qps with continuous streaming. This maps to ~1 dedicated slot for the pilot with 30% headroom for jitter when using continuous batching + prefix cache.
- Crest sizing: to hold P95 350ms on crest (60–85 qps) we’d provision burst capacity equivalent to ~6–8 concurrent slots (autoscaling with warm-pool). That covers the 7–12 minute crest windows and keeps cold-start exposure low.
- Token throughput: propose expressing pilot sizing in tokens/sec. For your peak crest mix we estimate ~55–75k tokens/sec aggregate (generation side). Spreadsheet breaks down tokens/sec by session percentile.
- Concurrency and streaming: your spike concurrency (180 concurrent streams) implies we should use parallel worker routing and connection-level keepalives. We recommend 90s idle timeout with a small sliding window to avoid premature KV cache eviction for multi-turn sessions.

Caveats & asks:
- We’ll need a representative sample of tokenized sessions (not just raw text) so our kernel selection and batching simulation can be accurate. If you can share 200 sample sessions across percentiles that will get us to +/-10% on the first-pass numbers.
- Confirm whether transcripts include long silence segments (they affect idle timeouts and memory residency).

Next steps:
1) You share tokenized samples / hourly CSV (you mentioned sending shortly).
2) We’ll run a quick micro-sim and return a pilot config (GPU types, slot counts, autoscale policy) within 48 business hours.
3) Align on canary window dates — suggest a short daytime 2-week canary once pilot infra is in place.

Attaching: throughput_matrix_vp.xlsx (spreadsheet), stream_profile_samples.json (sample traces).

— Olga
Olga Petrov
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference

From: Emma Liu <emma@velocitypay.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: VelocityPay Ops <ops@velocitypay.com>
Date: 2028-05-15T02:34:00Z
Subject: Re: Intro call follow-up: workload shape and SLOs

Thanks, Olga — attaching the 200-session tokenized sample + hourly QPS CSV as promised (uploaded to the Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0Bexample). A few clarifications after we reviewed your matrix: 

- The crest concurrency number we shared (180) includes background retries and non-customer triggered health-check pings. If you strip those out, user-triggered concurrency looks closer to 150. We left the 180 figure to be conservative.
- Silence segments: about 30% of sessions have 2–6s of silence between turns; about 4% have 15–30s pauses while agents wait for clarification. Those long pauses are the main reason we worried about idle timeouts.
- Canary window: target week of 2028-06-12 for the first daytime canary (business hours only). If Redwood can present a pilot config before 2028-05-19 that gives us time to align infra.

Also: for the fallback behavior — our customer experience team prefers: 1) trimmed response when latency crosses threshold, 2) then cached summary if degraded persists. We’d like Redwood to document the degradation path as part of the pilot runbook.

Best,
Emma

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-17T11:03:00Z
Subject: Internal: next steps & pilot config proposal (VelocityPay)

Olga — quick internal note to capture what we’ll deliver and owners before we send the scoped proposal to VelocityPay. 

Deliverables we’ll return to Emma by 2028-05-19: 
- Pilot capacity sheet (GPU types, reserved + burst slots, autoscale policy) — owner: Marissa. See spreadsheet tab "pilot_config" for numbers (13B quantized baseline, 8 steady slot equiv, 8 burst slot equiv).
- Detailed runbook: streaming keepalive, idle timeout rationale (propose 90s idle, 15s connection ping), KV cache warm policy, fallback sequence docs — owner: Karthik.
- Performance sim report: tokens/sec micro-sim showing expected P95 / P99 under crest distribution +/-10% — owner: Olga. We’ll include simulated traces from the provided 200 sessions.

Technical notes for the sim:
- Use conservative tokenization mapping (we assume whitespace-tokenizer + 4 tokens per English word avg for sampling).
- Model kernel selection: simulate quantized 13B path; estimate P95 for first-token under streaming as 270–380ms depending on concurrency window.
- Cache strategy: prefix cache on 30% of repeated prompts — this reduces effective tokens/sec by ~12% in steady-state.

Risks & mitigations:
- Crest > sustained: if crest spikes exceed 100 qps for >15m we’ll request temporary extra reserved capacity; propose an emergency escalation path in contract.
- Long-silence sessions increase memory residency; we’ll surface tail memory usage in the sim report.

I’ll draft the outbound email and attach the three artifacts for Olga to review before sending to Emma.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
